reconcile.connective: Defenders read the two commands as one mission in stages — restricted to Israel during Jesus' earthly ministry, then opened to all nations after the resurrection.

discrepancy.connective: Bart Ehrman presses the sharpest objection, arguing the universal Great Commission is an unhistorical post-Easter creation of the church that cannot be squared with the authentic, Israel-only restriction of the pre-Easter Jesus.

skeptic.name: Bart D. Ehrman
skeptic.work: Jesus: Apocalyptic Prophet of the New Millennium
skeptic.attribution: Bart D. Ehrman, Jesus: Apocalyptic Prophet of the New Millennium (Oxford University Press, 1999)

excerpts.excerpt_text: This restraint was upon them only in their first mission, afterwards they were appointed to go into all the world, and teach all nations.
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Directly resolves the tension by reading the Israel-only restriction (Matt 10:5-6) and the all-nations commission (Matt 28:19) as successive stages of a single mission — the harmonizing core of the row.

pd_work.resource: Matthew Henry, Commentary on the Whole Bible (1706-14), on Matthew 10:5
pd_work.author: Matthew Henry
pd_work.note: Henry treats this passage directly, framing the restriction as temporary ("only in their first mission") and superseded by the later commission to teach all nations.
